title: Let RAP save the order
intro: This behavior definition gives a custom order standard create and update operations.
context: Base behavior definition for an existing custom root CDS entity ZI_Order and table zorder. OrderUUID is a RAW(16) key; Comment is its business field. The generated global authorization handler must implement the application permissions.

highlights.label: RAP owns persistence
highlights.explanation: Managed RAP buffers changes and writes them to zorder during a successful save. You do not write the CRUD SQL yourself.

highlights.label: A technical key appears automatically
highlights.explanation: RAP generates the UUID during create. This is managed early numbering, not a final business document number assigned by a posting API.

highlights.label: Match CDS names to table columns
highlights.explanation: Comment in the business object is stored in order_comment. Mapping connects the two names.

outcome: Creating an order gives it a UUID; a successful save stores Comment in the mapped database column.
caveat: Teaching BDEF fragment, not a deployable BO. Strict-mode requirements, complete field mapping, authorization and service exposure must be completed for the target release.

references.title: SAP sample: managed behavior, numbering and mapping

title: Read the user's unsaved value
intro: EML reads the order that RAP is currently working on, including buffered changes.
context: Inside a handler of custom BO ZI_Order. Its generated keys parameter contains transactional keys; Order is the BDEF alias. This fragment reads data only.
code:
READ ENTITIES OF zi_order IN LOCAL MODE
  ENTITY Order
  FIELDS ( Comment )
  WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
  RESULT DATA(lt_orders)
  FAILED DATA(ls_failed)
  REPORTED DATA(ls_reported).

highlights.label: Read the buffer
highlights.explanation: If Comment was changed from Old to New in this transaction, this read can return New before the database is saved.

highlights.label: Keep the right instance
highlights.explanation: The incoming transactional key keeps draft identity when present. Local mode is allowed here because the code belongs to this BO's own implementation.

highlights.label: Check failed reads
highlights.explanation: Not every requested key must produce a result row. Use the failure and message responses when continuing the surrounding handler.

outcome: The next business rule uses the newly entered comment instead of an older database value.
caveat: Local mode bypasses specified BO access checks; it is not an authorization workaround for an external consumer. Response handling is outside this small read fragment.

title: An empty value can be an intentional update
intro: The control flag tells RAP to clear Comment instead of leaving it unchanged.
context: External EML consumer of non-draft custom BO ZI_Order, alias Order. order_uuid holds an existing UUID and Comment permits an empty value. The caller owns the later save decision.
code:
MODIFY ENTITIES OF zi_order
  ENTITY Order
  UPDATE FROM VALUE #(
    ( OrderUUID = order_uuid
      Comment = ''
      %control-Comment = if_abap_behv=>mk-on ) )
  FAILED DATA(ls_failed)
  REPORTED DATA(ls_reported).

highlights.label: Clear, do not ignore
highlights.explanation: An empty Comment plus mk-on means replace the old text with an empty value. An initial field without its control flag means it was not supplied.

highlights.label: Modification is not a save
highlights.explanation: First inspect failures and messages. A successful modify only updates the RAP transaction; the external caller still needs a save decision.

outcome: If the update and later save succeed, the old comment disappears.
caveat: Use the full transactional identity for draft or late-numbering scenarios. UPDATE FIELDS ( Comment ) WITH is another way to identify the intended field.

references.title: SAP samples: EML update fields and control

title: Save from the outer caller
intro: An external EML caller can save accepted changes; a RAP handler cannot commit them itself.
context: An external ABAP method after modifying custom BO ZI_Order. ls_failed is the preceding modify response. This example chooses to abandon the whole local transaction if any modification failed.
code:
IF ls_failed IS NOT INITIAL.
  ROLLBACK ENTITIES.
  RETURN.
ENDIF.
COMMIT ENTITIES RESPONSE OF zi_order
  FAILED DATA(ls_save_failed)
  REPORTED DATA(ls_save_reported).
DATA(save_subrc) = sy-subrc.
IF save_subrc <> 0.
  ROLLBACK ENTITIES.
ENDIF.

highlights.label: Choose the batch policy
highlights.explanation: This caller abandons all buffered changes after a failed modify. RAP does not make this the only possible policy for every mass operation.

highlights.label: Save has its own result
highlights.explanation: A modify can succeed and the save can still fail. Keep the save return code and responses instead of reporting success too early.

highlights.label: This caller gives up after save failure
highlights.explanation: Rollback clears the failed local transaction. For the supported late-save failure case with return code 8, rollback is required before continuing.

outcome: Only a successful commit is treated as a completed local save; unsuccessful transactions are abandoned.
caveat: Never paste this into a RAP handler or saver. Show the captured messages in the real caller. Rollback does not undo an independently committed remote request.

title: Connect a new item to its new order
intro: A temporary request label links the child to its parent before the caller knows the generated key.
context: External consumer of non-draft managed BO ZI_Order with alias Order and create-enabled composition _Items. Both order and item have managed UUID keys; only Comment and Quantity are required business fields in this small model.
code:
CONSTANTS co_order_cid TYPE abp_behv_cid VALUE 'O1'.
CONSTANTS co_item_cid TYPE abp_behv_cid VALUE 'I1'.
MODIFY ENTITIES OF zi_order
  ENTITY Order
  CREATE FIELDS ( Comment )
  WITH VALUE #( ( %cid = co_order_cid Comment = '' ) )
  CREATE BY \_Items FIELDS ( Quantity )
  WITH VALUE #(
    ( %cid_ref = co_order_cid
      %target = VALUE #(
        ( %cid = co_item_cid Quantity = 2 ) ) ) )
  MAPPED DATA(ls_mapped)
  FAILED DATA(ls_failed)
  REPORTED DATA(ls_reported).

highlights.label: O1 means this new parent
highlights.explanation: The child's %cid_ref points to the parent's %cid within this request. O1 is not a database key.

highlights.label: Create through the composition
highlights.explanation: CREATE BY _Items creates an item under that order. The item gets its own request label I1.

highlights.label: Map labels to returned keys
highlights.explanation: MAPPED connects successful creates to their generated identities. FAILED identifies rejected operations and REPORTED carries messages.

outcome: One request creates an order and its quantity-2 item in the RAP buffer with the correct parent-child relationship.
caveat: Inspect all responses before deciding to save. Draft creates need draft identity; late numbering adds preliminary-key handling not shown here.

references.title: SAP samples: EML content IDs and create by association

title: Tell RAP when to check the dates
intro: A validation belongs in the behavior definition so every relevant save path runs the rule.
context: Fragment inside the entity body of a managed, draft-enabled Order BDEF. BeginDate and EndDate exist. The generated validateDates handler implements the date check.

highlights.label: Cover creation and both inputs
highlights.explanation: The rule is triggered for a newly created order and changes to either date. It is not just a check in one screen's button handler.

highlights.label: Include draft preparation
highlights.explanation: Prepare includes the validation for draft preparation. The on-save rule still matters for applicable active-data save paths.

outcome: An order with EndDate before BeginDate can be rejected by its validation before it is persisted.
caveat: Merge into the existing Prepare declaration rather than adding a second one. Do not depend on a fixed execution order or on a rule running only once.

references.title: SAP sample: validation and draft Prepare

title: Reject the order and explain the reason
intro: FAILED stops the invalid instance; REPORTED tells the user what to fix.
context: Inside Order's validateDates handler, after an EML read of BeginDate and EndDate into lt_orders. The named constants co_state_dates, co_message_id and co_bad_dates identify a state area and a translatable message-class error.
code:
LOOP AT lt_orders INTO DATA(ls_order).
  APPEND VALUE #(
    %tky = ls_order-%tky
    %state_area = co_state_dates ) TO reported-order.
  IF ls_order-EndDate < ls_order-BeginDate.
    APPEND VALUE #( %tky = ls_order-%tky )
      TO failed-order.
    APPEND VALUE #(
      %tky = ls_order-%tky
      %state_area = co_state_dates
      %element-EndDate = if_abap_behv=>mk-on
      %msg = new_message(
        id = co_message_id
        number = co_bad_dates
        severity = if_abap_behv_message=>severity-error ) )
      TO reported-order.
  ENDIF.
ENDLOOP.

highlights.label: Clear the previous check result
highlights.explanation: The empty state-area entry invalidates the old date message for this instance before the rule is evaluated again.

highlights.label: Reject this instance
highlights.explanation: When the end date is too early, the transactional key is added to FAILED. An error message alone is not the rejection.

highlights.label: Point to the field to fix
highlights.explanation: The reported error is attached to this order and its EndDate field. After correction, the old state message is cleared and no replacement error is added.

outcome: The invalid order cannot be saved, and the user sees a date error on the correct order; correcting the dates clears it on revalidation.
caveat: Draft-enabled root example. Include this validation in Prepare. Child errors also need the appropriate path to their parent; initial dates need a separate rule if they are forbidden.

title: Recalculate instead of adding twice
intro: A determination should produce the same total when RAP runs it again with the same inputs.
context: Inside an Order determination of custom managed BO ZI_Order. The BDEF triggers it on create and changes to Quantity or UnitPrice. Total is derived and read-only to external consumers; numeric fields use suitable decimal types.
code:
READ ENTITIES OF zi_order IN LOCAL MODE
  ENTITY Order
  FIELDS ( Quantity UnitPrice )
  WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
  RESULT DATA(lt_orders).
MODIFY ENTITIES OF zi_order IN LOCAL MODE
  ENTITY Order
  UPDATE FIELDS ( Total )
  WITH VALUE #( FOR ls_order IN lt_orders
    ( %tky = ls_order-%tky
      Total = ls_order-Quantity * ls_order-UnitPrice ) )
  REPORTED DATA(ls_reported).
APPEND LINES OF ls_reported-order TO reported-order.

highlights.label: Read the current inputs
highlights.explanation: Use the transaction's current quantity and price, including unsaved edits.

highlights.label: Replace the total
highlights.explanation: Quantity 3 and price 10 produce Total 30 every time. Adding 30 to the old total would incorrectly produce 60 on a second run.

highlights.label: Only trusted derived input
highlights.explanation: Local mode updates readonly Total from Quantity and UnitPrice. A public action that instead passes an arbitrary caller-supplied Total can create an indirect write bypass. Check input and permissions at the public operation boundary.

outcome: The buffered Total becomes 30 for quantity 3 and unit price 10, regardless of repeated execution with those inputs.
caveat: Focused formula fragment; production code needs currency rounding and response handling appropriate to the actual BO. Determinations have no FAILED output and do not replace rejecting validations.

title: Return the changed order from an action
intro: Changing an order and returning the action result are two separate steps.
context: Tail of an instance action handler for Order with BDEF declaration action Approve result [1] $self. The preceding update has already succeeded for lt_successful_keys, a table of transactional keys; failures and messages have already been collected.
code:
READ ENTITIES OF zi_order IN LOCAL MODE
  ENTITY Order
  ALL FIELDS
  WITH CORRESPONDING #( lt_successful_keys )
  RESULT DATA(lt_orders)
  FAILED DATA(ls_read_failed)
  REPORTED DATA(ls_read_reported).
result = VALUE #( FOR ls_order IN lt_orders
  ( %tky = ls_order-%tky
    %param = ls_order ) ).

highlights.label: Read the changed data
highlights.explanation: Read the successful instances from the transaction after changing their status. Do not return the old input rows as the result.

highlights.label: Fill the declared result
highlights.explanation: %tky identifies the action's instance and %param contains its returned order data for the declared $self result.

outcome: A successful Approve result contains the newly approved order data instead of an empty response.
caveat: Only the result-building step is shown; merge read failures/messages into the surrounding action responses. A copy or factory action needs its own declared create/result contract; this instance-action fragment does not implement CopyOrder.

references.title: SAP sample: instance actions and $self results

title: Choose which operations the service exposes
intro: A projection reuses selected behavior from the underlying business object.
context: Projection behavior for custom CDS projection ZC_Order over ZI_Order. The underlying behavior already defines create, update and Approve; both behaviors use strict mode 2. This is a non-draft example.

highlights.label: This is the consumer-facing layer
highlights.explanation: ZC_Order projects the underlying order BO. It does not implement a second database save.

highlights.label: Expose selected operations
highlights.explanation: The consumer gets create, update and Approve from the base behavior. An operation missing from the underlying behavior cannot be invented by writing use here.

outcome: The projected BO offers these selected operations to its consumers.
caveat: A projection is not automatically a released SAP BO interface. Check the actual object's release contract before cross-component or SAP API consumption.

title: Give the entity its service name
intro: The service definition selects entities; the service binding supplies the protocol.
context: Service definition ZUI_Order for an existing custom transactional projection ZC_Order. Create the appropriate service binding as a separate ADT repository object.

highlights.label: Publish this entity shape
highlights.explanation: The service includes ZC_Order under the external entity name Orders.

highlights.label: No OData version appears here
highlights.explanation: OData V4 UI or Web API is selected in a service binding, not in this definition. Activation of this source alone does not create a usable endpoint.

outcome: A matching published binding can expose the Orders entity with its projected fields and supported behavior.
caveat: Service access, binding publication, communication setup and UI annotations are separate tasks; available binding types depend on the target product and release.

title: Two timestamps protect two different checks
intro: The entity ETag checks stale updates; the total ETag protects draft transitions against active changes.
context: Selected declarations from a managed draft Order BDEF. The full BDEF already has with draft, its persistent table, operations and readonly fields. zorder_d is a generated draft table; both timestamp fields have the proper CDS administrative annotations.

highlights.label: Check this entity version
highlights.explanation: LocalLastChangedAt supports the consumer's optimistic update check for the entity.

highlights.label: Detect relevant active BO changes
highlights.explanation: LastChangedAt is the total ETag. If the active BO changed while a draft lock was no longer protecting it, a stale draft must not silently replace that newer state.

highlights.label: Separate draft work from active data
highlights.explanation: Edit starts draft editing, Activate attempts the active save, Discard drops draft work and Resume continues editing an existing draft.

outcome: A stale client or stale draft can be rejected instead of overwriting a newer active change.
caveat: Two insertion regions are shown, not a complete BDEF. Keep child lock dependencies and timestamp maintenance correct; include relevant validations in the existing Prepare declaration.

references.title: SAP sample: draft and ETag declarations

title: Tell the UI to reload Total
intro: A side effect refreshes a value on the screen after another value changes.
context: First block: inside the base Order BDEF entity body. Final line: inside its projection BDEF entity body. Quantity and Total exist; a backend determination already recalculates Total.

highlights.label: A UI refresh dependency
highlights.explanation: When the user changes Quantity, the UI is told that Total should be read again.

highlights.label: Expose it to the consumer
highlights.explanation: The projection reuses the base side-effect rules so a supporting consumer can receive them.

outcome: After Quantity changes from 2 to 3, a supporting Fiori consumer reloads the backend Total and displays the new value.
caveat: This does not calculate Total, save data or replace authorization. Verify RAP side-effect support and the generated metadata for the target binding and UI.

title: Items belong to the order's composition tree
intro: A composition models the child entities that belong to one business object.
context: Root CDS entity for custom table zorder. ZI_OrderItem already declares an association to parent ZI_Order as _Order, with its parent UUID join. Activate the dependent CDS definitions together.
code:
define root view entity ZI_Order
  as select from zorder
  composition [0..*] of ZI_OrderItem as _Items
{
  key order_uuid as OrderUUID,
      order_comment as Comment,
      _Items
}

highlights.label: One root, several children
highlights.explanation: An order can own zero or more item instances in its BO tree. The child needs a matching association back to the parent.

highlights.label: Expose the navigation
highlights.explanation: Including _Items in the element list makes the composition available in the CDS model. The BDEF separately enables create-by-association and defines lock and authorization dependencies.

outcome: The model has an Order-to-Items composition that RAP behavior can use for parent-child operations.
caveat: Composition syntax alone does not provide an entire transactional BO, cross-system atomicity or the required access-control design.

references.title: SAP sample: parent and child composition model

title: Return an authorization decision for Update
intro: The authorization handler decides whether the caller may request an operation.
context: Inside Order's generated get_global_authorizations handler; its BDEF declares authorization master ( global ). update_allowed is an abap_bool already obtained from the application's real authorization check, not from a UI flag.
code:
IF requested_authorizations-%update =
   if_abap_behv=>mk-on.
  result-%update = COND #(
    WHEN update_allowed = abap_true
    THEN if_abap_behv=>auth-allowed
    ELSE if_abap_behv=>auth-unauthorized ).
ENDIF.

highlights.label: Answer the requested operation
highlights.explanation: The framework asks for Update authorization. Only fill this decision when it was requested.

highlights.label: Allow or deny explicitly
highlights.explanation: The result uses RAP's authorization constants. A disabled button is not this server-side permission decision.

outcome: A caller without update permission receives an unauthorized decision even if it bypasses the screen.
caveat: The real authority check, draft Edit and other requested operations must be implemented too. An action declared authorization:none is not protected by simply filling this Update result.

references.title: SAP samples: RAP global and instance authorization

title: Return the total count before cutting the page
intro: The total count describes all matching rows, while the data response contains only the requested page.
context: Inside IF_RAP_QUERY_PROVIDER~SELECT for a small in-memory demonstration. lt_all is a standard table of the query result type, already filtered, authorized and sorted exactly as requested, with a unique tie-breaker. lt_page has the same table type.
code:
IF io_request->is_total_numb_of_rec_requested( ).
  io_response->set_total_number_of_records( lines( lt_all ) ).
ENDIF.
IF io_request->is_data_requested( ).
  DATA(paging) = io_request->get_paging( ).
  DATA(page_size) = paging->get_page_size( ).
  DATA(offset) = paging->get_offset( ).
  CLEAR lt_page.
  LOOP AT lt_all INTO DATA(ls_row).
    IF sy-tabix <= offset.
      CONTINUE.
    ENDIF.
    IF page_size <> if_rap_query_paging=>page_size_unlimited
       AND lines( lt_page ) >= page_size.
      EXIT.
    ENDIF.
    APPEND ls_row TO lt_page.
  ENDLOOP.
  io_response->set_data( lt_page ).
ENDIF.

highlights.label: Count the full authorized result
highlights.explanation: Lea can read matching orders 101, 104, 108 and 110. Return count 4 even when she requests only two rows.

highlights.label: Apply skip and top
highlights.explanation: Skip the requested offset, then stop at the page size. Size zero returns no data; the unlimited constant does not impose a size limit.

highlights.label: Send just this page
highlights.explanation: With skip 1 and top 2, return orders 104 and 108 from that same authorized and consistently ordered result.

outcome: The page contains orders 104 and 108; the total count remains 4.
caveat: This teaches response shaping, not a complete query provider. Apply filters, authorization, requested sorting, search and supported aggregation before paging; push work to the data source for large result sets.

title: Expose one new field through an allowed extension
intro: Adding a field to the consumer projection is one step of extending a business object.
context: A CDS view-entity extension for your own ZC_Order projection over ZI_Order. Your table and base entity already contain ApprovalReference, persistence mapping is maintained, and ZC_Order permits this extension in the target release. This is not an SAP standard BO.

highlights.label: Extend the permitted layer
highlights.explanation: The extension adds to the existing projection. Before writing it, verify that this exact entity is allowed to be extended.

highlights.label: Expose an existing base field
highlights.explanation: ApprovalReference already exists below the projection. This line makes it part of the projection's field list; it does not create a table column or implement a validation.

outcome: After activating compatible objects, the projection includes ApprovalReference. Verify the field in service metadata, then test read, update and save through the real service.
caveat: For an SAP BO, use only its released extension points and supported names. Also check persistence, BDEF extension support, field permissions, validation, UI metadata and old consumers; this snippet alone does not prove end-to-end extensibility.

title: A late number is assigned during save
intro: Late numbering tells RAP that the final business key is not available during the initial create.
context: Selected regions of a custom managed Order BDEF using business document number OrderNumber as its key, assigned by ADJUST_NUMBERS during save. The behavior implementation includes the required ADJUST_NUMBERS saver logic. This alternative model is separate from the UUID-numbered examples.

highlights.label: Declare the timing
highlights.explanation: New instances use preliminary identity until the save sequence assigns their final key. The saver must map preliminary identity to the actual returned number.

highlights.label: Do not ask the caller to invent the key
highlights.explanation: The consumer creates an order without supplying OrderNumber. It must not treat a temporary label as the final posting number.

outcome: The model can represent a newly created order before its final document number is known.
caveat: Declaration only: it does not implement ADJUST_NUMBERS or make a self-committing API safe. Draft requires suitable preliminary-key modeling; BAPI integration and late-save failure support depend on the target release.

references.title: SAP: BAPI numbering and save sequence

title: Keep an amount beside its currency
intro: A number such as 100 is not a complete monetary amount until its currency is known.
context: Custom CDS view entity over zorder, with a suitable amount column total_amount and currency column currency_code. This is a data-model fragment, not an analytical query.

highlights.label: Name the currency field
highlights.explanation: The annotation links TotalAmount to CurrencyCode in the same entity. A consumer can distinguish 100 EUR from 100 USD.

highlights.label: This is meaning, not conversion
highlights.explanation: The annotation does not convert USD to EUR. Group by currency or perform an explicitly defined conversion before combining mixed-currency amounts.

outcome: The service can describe an amount together with its currency instead of presenting an unexplained number.
caveat: Do not assume a plain SQL SUM respects currency semantics automatically. Conversion requires the intended rate type, rate date, target currency and error policy.

references.title: SAP: amount and currency semantics in CDS

title: Join only the text language you need
intro: A complete text join avoids turning one order into several language rows.
context: Custom zorder has one row per order_uuid and a status column. ZI_StatusText has a genuine unique key of Status plus Language and a Description field; its Language uses the session language format.
code:
define view entity ZI_OrderText
  as select from zorder as Orders
  association [0..1] to ZI_StatusText as _Text
    on Orders.status = _Text.Status
    and _Text.Language = $session.system_language
{
  key Orders.order_uuid as OrderUUID,
      Orders.status as Status,
      _Text.Description as StatusText
}

highlights.label: Match both parts of the text key
highlights.explanation: Matching only Status could find English, German and French rows. The language condition selects the current language.

highlights.label: Cardinality must match real data
highlights.explanation: With at most one text row per status and language, selecting StatusText preserves one row per order. Writing [0..1] or key does not remove duplicate data.

outcome: An order with status texts in EN and DE still appears once when its text is selected for one language.
caveat: Missing text can remain empty; fallback-language logic is separate. Verify all key dimensions and the actual source uniqueness rather than using DISTINCT to hide an incomplete join.

references.title: SAP sample: text association with session language

title: Put display hints in the metadata extension
intro: UI annotations describe how a field is displayed without changing how the order is saved.
context: Metadata extension for your own ZC_Order, which has @Metadata.allowExtensions: true. OrderNumber exists. This project uses CORE for its own base application metadata, not as a blanket layer choice for extending SAP applications.

highlights.label: Annotate the existing entity
highlights.explanation: The metadata extension targets ZC_Order. It adds presentation information rather than creating another BO or table.

highlights.label: Show the field in the UI
highlights.explanation: LineItem describes list display and Identification describes an identification field. The position helps order these fields for a supporting Fiori elements consumer.

outcome: A supporting UI can show OrderNumber in the list and identification area using the service metadata.
caveat: Only annotations permitted in metadata extensions may be used there. The actual page layout also depends on facets and UI configuration; annotation layers control precedence, not authorization.

references.title: SAP: metadata extensions and allowed annotations

title: Protect the entity that the consumer actually reads
intro: A higher CDS entity does not automatically inherit the lower entity's read restrictions.
context: DCL access control for custom ZC_Order over ZI_Order. ZI_Order already has the intended DCL; ZC_Order uses #CHECK and exposes all authorization-relevant fields under compatible names. No other role grants broader access in this example.

highlights.label: Protect the consumed entity
highlights.explanation: This rule names ZC_Order, which the consumer reads. A rule only on ZI_Order does not automatically protect reads of ZC_Order.

highlights.label: Reuse the lower conditions explicitly
highlights.explanation: The inheritance condition applies the existing ZI_Order restrictions to this compatible model. Renamed or changed field paths may require explicit replacement mappings.

outcome: A normal DCL-protected read of ZC_Order applies the inherited row restrictions, rather than showing every order.
caveat: Test with restricted business users through the actual consumer. CDS read checks do not replace RAP operation authorization, and privileged reads or broader DCL grants need separate review.

references.title: SAP: CDS access control and nonautomatic inheritance
